CapabilityValue.description:
What a Provider declares it can do for a key (spec 05 `ProviderInstance`).

Rule: SB-6.

DataContractId.description:
A namespaced contract id matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$`,
for example `ezsdr.stream.cf32`.

Rule: SC-2.

Namespace.description:
A dotted sequence of [`Ident`]s owned by a Vocabulary or a Module,
matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)*$`.

Rule: SB-1.

NodeId.description:
A node in the (future) multi-host deployment. `LOCAL` is the only legal value in v4.0.

Rule: X7 (`00-overview.md`); it qualifies every id of TM-11, SC-6, SB-3 and MA-19.

Port.description:
A name, a direction and a contract id, and nothing more. Per-port parameters
the Kernel does not interpret — a tensor shape, a maximum PDU length — live in
the `ComponentDescriptor`'s parameters (MA-36), not here.

Rule: SC-1.

direction.description: Whether the component consumes or produces here (SC-1).

name.description: Port name, unique within its component (MA-37).

PortDirection.description: Which way samples flow through a [`Port`] (SC-1).

ResourceId.description:
Names a resource, or a sub-resource, inside the composite tree a Provider declares.

The path is a non-empty sequence of segments; `dev0/rx/0` names channel 0 of the
receive sub-tree of `dev0`. Vision §49 asks only for the node qualification; the
path replaces §49's flat `local` because a channel or a timekeeper must be
addressable (`00-overview.md` "Where these specs depart from the Vision").

Rule: SB-33, SB-34 (`03-spec-and-binding.md`), X7.

path.description: Slash-joined path through the composite resource tree (SB-34).

anyOf.description: A signed 64-bit integer, written as an exact decimal by the canonicaliser (OV-15).

A finite float; a non-finite one is refused rather than written as `null`,
because a `Value` reaches the sealed Manifest through `prepare.effective`,
the coercion records and the action log (OV-15, X9).
A list of scalars; nesting deeper is refused (SB-4).
A map of scalars; nesting deeper is refused (SB-4).

Value.description:
A scalar, or a list or map of scalars nested at most one level.

A Spec is data, not a document tree: one level is what a structured parameter
such as a capture request needs, and more invites the schema-inside-a-schema
that Vision §9 rejects.

Rule: SB-4.

description:
One node of a Provider's composite resource tree: a device with channels,
streams, a timekeeper, GPIO banks and sensors beneath it, each with its own
`ResourceId` and its own declared capabilities.

Rule: MA-10, SB-33.

capabilities.description: What it declares it can do (SB-6).

id.description: This node's address in the tree (SB-3).

kind.description: What kind of node it is; a Spec resource's `kind` must match (SB-34).

ports.description:
The Ports this node carries, for a node that is a stream endpoint. A Spec
links a component to a bound resource through one of these, which is how
Vision §7's `PHY Processor -> SampleStream -> Radio Port` is expressible;
without them `PortRef.component` could name a resource but no contract
could be checked against it (MA-10, SB-15, SC-1, SC-3).

shareable.description:
Whether more than one Spec resource may bind to this node. Default `false`:
a channel or a stream is exclusive, while Vision §8's GPIO banks "may share
the timekeeper" of §39, so which is which is the Provider's declaration and
never the Kernel's knowledge (MA-10, SB-34, OV-21).
